name: Direct Relief: medical aid abroad (donated medicines and grants)
beneficiaries_note: Our build: international material aid by value (Ukraine $535m and the Middle East $193m of $1,633m, Sudan $23m, Haiti $12m: annual report FY2025 pp. 25-26, 43); the rest, about half, spread over Direct Relief's partners in Latin America, Africa and Asia (a judgment, its own reports name no split): the shares are of aid, a stand-in for the shares of the result.
summary: Direct Relief ships medicines and supplies that manufacturers donate, requested by health facilities, ministries and NGOs abroad, $1.6 billion at US wholesale value in the year to June 2025 (a third to Ukraine, an eighth to the Middle East), and gives $31m in grants to local health partners. This model values the medicines at local prices and the health they buy at what the recipient health systems' next dollar buys (a cost per DALY of about 30% of income per person), deaths valued by age, and credits Direct Relief with its own cash's share of the resources behind them, the donated goods being the manufacturers'; the grants count in full. The result, about 0.4 years of healthy life per $1,000, rests on judgments: how useful donated, often short-dated and branded stock is against the health system's marginal spending, and what the goods are worth locally. Both branches, medicines and grants, are discounted by the shared missing-data slider: nothing measures the health these medicines produce.

source.title: charityevals' estimate: Direct Relief, medical aid abroad (fiscal 2025)

sections.title: Cost
sections.explainer: What the modelled program cost in the year the outcomes below are counted for, including its share of overhead. From audited financial statements or the annual report.

sections.title: Reach
sections.explainer: How many people, animals or meals the spending reached in the same year, as the charity reports it.

sections.title: Effect per unit
sections.explainer: What the intervention does for each unit reached, from the best available studies, before any adjustment.

sections.title: Adjustments
sections.explainer: Discounts for weaker evidence, what would have happened anyway, credit shared with others, and delivery falling short. All multiply the outcome.

sections.title: Other outcomes, in this model's unit
sections.explainer: charityevals' standard step for outcomes in more than one unit (docs/normalization.md 2.6): each outcome is counted in its own unit (units of value for income and deaths, WELLBYs for life satisfaction, tonnes of CO₂e, chicken pain days) and put into this model's unit by its unit's conversion over this unit's, which the headline's conversion cancels. So each moves only with its own sliders, exactly as in a model of its own unit. The rows are fixed; don't edit them.

sections.title: Outcome
sections.explainer: The outcome in the family's shared unit, per dollar.

sections.title: Your dollar's share
sections.explainer: Staff who earn less than they could elsewhere pay part of the cost in kind. With credit by share of resources, your dollar is credited with its share of the full cost only.

source.title: Direct Relief and Affiliates, Report of Independent Auditors and Consolidated Financial Statements, June 30, 2025 and 2024 (Baker Tilly, audited)

rows.explainer: Direct Relief's own spending on its international programme in the year to 30 June 2025, the latest with audited accounts: grants, bought medicines, freight, warehousing, staff and the rest. The international column, $1,890,911k, less donated goods distributed ($1,621,563k), expired donated stock written off ($197,863k, a non-cash write-off at wholesale value) and donated freight ($1,302k). rows.label: Patient-years of medicine delivered abroad (defined daily doses ÷ 365)
rows.explainer: Reach as years of treatment: the year's defined daily doses abroad over 365. Direct Relief doesn't count patients; its partners (health facilities, ministries and NGOs in 92 countries) do the dispensing.

rows.explainer: Context: Direct Relief's own cash per patient-year of medicine its partners received.

rows.explainer: Not used: the death rate the medicines change is not measured; deaths averted come from the health-system figure instead (deaths_averted_per_person).

rows.explainer: Not used: the death rate the medicines change is not measured; deaths averted come from the health-system figure instead (deaths_averted_per_person).

rows.explainer: Not used: the death rate the medicines change is not measured; deaths averted come from the health-system figure instead (deaths_averted_per_person).

rows.explainer: One: reach is already counted in patient-years of treatment.

rows.label: Deaths averted per patient-year of medicine (before adjustments)
rows.formula: goods_local_value / people_reached * need_vs_marginal / cost_per_daly * (1 - yld_share) * deaths_per_daly
rows.explainer: The local value of the medicines per patient-year over the recipient health systems' cost per DALY, times the need ratio, the share that is deaths, times deaths per DALY.

rows.label: Share of the deaths averted that are of children under five
rows.explainer: Ukraine's and the Middle East's patients are mostly adults with chronic illness or injuries; partners in Africa, Haiti and Latin America treat child infections, and the midwife and perinatal kits newborns. Our judgment, 25% (10% to 40%).

rows.label: Of the deaths averted at five or older, share aged 5 to 14
rows.explainer: Few deaths at these ages in any recipient country. Our judgment, 5% (2% to 12%).

rows.label: Of the deaths averted at 15 or older, share aged 15 to 49
rows.explainer: Chronic-disease deaths (insulin, cancer drugs, cardiovascular medicines) are mostly at 50 and over; maternal deaths and war injuries at 15 to 49. Our judgment, 30% (15% to 45%).

rows.label: Value of a death averted (units of value)
rows.explainer: The site's one value of a death, by age band, times your value of a life (multiplied by zero deaths here).

rows.label: Goods valued as income (none)
rows.explainer: Zero: medicines are valued only as the health they produce (below), so nothing is counted again as income.

rows.label: PPP conversion (2017 international $ per US $), Ukraine
rows.explainer: Ukraine's fact, the largest recipient; multiplied by zero goods valued as income.

rows.label: Consumption per person per year, Ukraine (not used)
rows.explainer: Ukraine's fact; multiplied by zero goods valued as income.

rows.label: ln(consumption) gain per person (none)
rows.explainer: Zero, as no goods are valued as income.

rows.label: Local market value of the donated goods ÷ their US wholesale value

source.title: Mulcahy, Schwam, Lovejoy (RAND, 2024), International Prescription Drug Price Comparisons: Estimates Using 2022 Data, RAND Health Quarterly 11(3)
source.quote: U.S. prices for brand-name originator drugs were 422 percent of prices in comparison countries.

rows.explainer: In-kind gifts are valued at local market prices, not donor list prices (families/humanitarian-relief.md). Direct Relief books donated drugs at US wholesale acquisition cost (European branded products discounted, p. 15). Anchor: US manufacturer prices were 422% of 33 OECD countries' for brand-name drugs (ratio 0.24) and 67% for unbranded generics (ratio about 1.5), 278% across all drugs (0.36); the poorer recipients buy generics cheaper still, through tenders and international suppliers. Most of the value Direct Relief books is branded product (insulin, oncology, cystic fibrosis drugs). Our judgment, 0.3.

rows.label: Medicines and supplies delivered abroad, at local market value
rows.explainer: The donated goods at local prices plus what Direct Relief bought (at cost).

rows.explainer: The other two thirds went to the Middle East ($193m: Gaza, Lebanon, Syria, annual report p. 26), Sudan ($23m), Haiti ($12m) and partners in Latin America, Africa and Asia (Mexico, Guatemala, Honduras, Uganda, Nigeria, Kenya, India, the Philippines, Malawi, Sierra Leone). Because the health bought is value over cost per DALY, countries are pooled by the harmonic mean of income, which the poorer recipients pull down. Anchor: World Bank 2024 incomes weighted by the beneficiary split give $1,985 (harmonic; $4,664 arithmetic); group averages are $2,354 for lower-middle income, $10,443 upper-middle, $809 low income. Our judgment, $2,000 ($1,200 to $4,000).

rows.label: Recipients' GDP per person, aid-weighted harmonic mean
rows.explainer: Ukraine's share of the aid at Ukraine's income, the rest at the others'; harmonic, since DALYs bought are value divided by cost per DALY.

rows.label: Cost of a DALY averted by recipients' health spending at the margin, as a share of GDP per person

source.title: Woods, Revill, Sculpher, Claxton (2016), Country-Level Cost-Effectiveness Thresholds: Initial Estimates and the Need for Further Research, Value in Health 19(8)

rows.explainer: What the recipient health systems' next dollar buys in health (the supply-side threshold): the right price of a DALY for medicines that either free a facility's budget or add care at its margin. Anchors: Woods et al. (2016) estimate 1–51% of GDP per person for Malawi, 4–51% for Cambodia, 11–51% for El Salvador and 32–59% for Kazakhstan; Ochalek et al. (2018), for 123 low- and middle-income countries, find few above 1× GDP per person. Our judgment, 30%.

rows.label: Recipient health systems' cost per DALY averted at the margin (US$)
rows.explainer: GDP per person times the threshold share.

rows.label: Share of the DALYs bought at the margin that are illness (not deaths)
rows.explainer: The shared figure for medicines in low- and middle-income health systems (facts/death_ages.json): the rest are deaths, valued by age.

rows.label: Deaths per DALY of years of life lost
rows.explainer: The shared figure (facts/death_ages.json): turns the years of life lost back into deaths, so each is valued by age at the site's value of a death.

rows.label: Health gained per dollar of these medicines ÷ per marginal dollar of the health system
rows.explainer: Direct Relief ships what partners request, much of it to places where supply has broken down (Ukraine's war, Gaza, Sudan, Haiti, hurricane-hit islands), where medicines save more than the health system's least valuable spending (+). Against that, the mix follows what manufacturers give: short-dated and branded stock, specialty products whose local value overstates what they do for the people treated, things a facility would not have bought (−). Unlike the US model (1.5), the threshold here is already the whole system's marginal spending in poor countries, where medicines are among the inputs most often missing. Our judgment, 1 (0.5 to 2.5).

rows.label: Illness averted per patient-year of medicine, in DALYs (before adjustments)
rows.explainer: The same health bought, its years lived with disability: the share not lost to death.

rows.label: Grants: health gained per dollar ÷ per marginal dollar of the health system
rows.explainer: The grants fund local organisations' care: rehabilitation and mobile clinics in Ukraine, earthquake recovery and mental health in Turkey and Syria, maternal care, solar power for clinics, warehousing in the Middle East. Some is less directly health (solar systems, logistics, heat-risk data); the rest is care in crisis settings. Our judgment, 0.8.

rows.label: Grants for the crisis in Ukraine, fiscal 2025

source.title: Direct Relief, Fiscal Year 2025 Annual Report (July 2024 to June 2025)
source.quote: including the crisis in Ukraine ($19.7 million)

rows.explainer: The largest part of the international grants, weighting their cost per DALY.

rows.label: Grants: recipients' cost per DALY at the margin (US$)
rows.explainer: Ukraine's share of the grants at Ukraine's income, the rest (Turkey and Syria, Israel and Palestine, and others) at the other recipients', harmonic, times the threshold share.

rows.label: Grants: illness averted, in DALYs (before adjustments)
rows.explainer: The grants over the recipients' cost per DALY, times the need ratio, the share not lost to death.

rows.label: Grants: deaths averted (before adjustments)
rows.explainer: The grants' health bought, the share that is deaths, times deaths per DALY.

rows.label: Medicines: illness averted, in DALYs (before adjustments)
rows.explainer: Patient-years times illness DALYs per patient-year.

rows.label: Evidence adjustment (bias in the threshold's health per dollar), a multiplier
rows.explainer: The cost per DALY comes from cross-country estimates of how health spending changes mortality (Ochalek et al.; Woods et al.). Such estimates can be biased either way (spending follows need, which hides its effect; or richer countries spend and live longer for other reasons); we know of no evidence of a net direction. That the outcome isn't measured for these medicines is in the missing-data step. 1 (0.8 to 1.1).

rows.label: Share of the outcome that wouldn't have happened without Direct Relief
rows.explainer: Medicines: other channels deliver donated medicines too (Americares, Project HOPE, MAP International; WHO and UNICEF supply in Ukraine and Gaza), so some of the same products would have reached the same patients. (Products a partner would have bought free its budget, which the cost per DALY at the margin already values.) Grants: some partners would have found other funders; Ukraine's response was well funded, Sudan's and Haiti's were not. Our judgment, 0.75 (0.5 to 0.9) for both branches.

rows.label: Medicines: Direct Relief's share of the resources behind them
rows.formula: (program_spend - int_grants) * overhead_ratio / ((program_spend - int_grants) * overhead_ratio + int_donated_goods * price_ratio_local)
rows.explainer: Convention 2: the cash Direct Relief spends to source, store, ship and follow up (its international programme less grants, with overhead) over that cash plus the donated goods at local value, the manufacturers' resources. The recipient facilities' staff time is inside the health-system cost per DALY, which prices everything a marginal dollar buys.

rows.label: Grants: Direct Relief's share of the resources
rows.explainer: One: the grant buys care at the health system's cost per DALY, which includes every input; the partner's other funds buy their own DALYs.

rows.label: Share of credit used (outcome-weighted average of the branches, for reading only)
rows.explainer: Outcome-weighted average of the branches, for reading only.

rows.label: Medicines: share dispensed to patients before they expire
rows.explainer: Much donated stock is short-dated (Direct Relief writes off its own expired stock in its warehouse, $197.9m abroad in fiscal 2025, audited accounts p. 7: that never reaches partners and is not in the goods counted here). Some of what partners receive still expires on their shelves or is not what their patients need. Our judgment, 0.85 (0.7 to 0.95).

rows.label: Grants: share spent as planned
rows.explainer: Grants go to vetted partners with milestone reviews before further payments (audited accounts p. 14). Our judgment, 0.9.

rows.label: Leverage and funging
rows.explainer: No government money is involved (Direct Relief takes none); a donation neither displaces nor draws in other funders' money much. 1.

rows.label: Years a gift waits before it is spent
rows.explainer: The shared Direct Relief figure (facts/direct_relief.json), read by both models.

rows.label: Years from shipment to the medicines' use
rows.explainer: No study measures the lag from shipment to use, so the reference class is the rule for it: WHO's guidelines for drug donations ask for at least a year of shelf life on arrival, 'to allow for the all too frequent in-country distribution delays'. Direct Relief ships to partner facilities that dispense the medicines themselves, so less than that year: a quarter of a year (0 to half a year).

rows.label: Half of the year over which a patient-year of medicine is taken
rows.explainer: The medicines are taken over the year after delivery; the middle of it is half a year on.

rows.label: Discount for the wait
rows.explainer: The gift's wait, the delivery and the middle of the year of treatment, discounted at the shared rate.

rows.label: Medicines: counted less where the outcome isn't measured
rows.explainer: Thin (Convention 12): Direct Relief counts doses delivered, but the health they produce is a judgment through the health system's cost per DALY, not measured for these medicines.

rows.label: Grants: counted less where the outcome isn't measured
rows.explainer: Thin: no outcome data for the grant-funded care.

rows.label: Counted less where the outcome isn't measured (outcome-weighted average of the branches, for reading only)
rows.explainer: Outcome-weighted average of the branches, for reading only.

rows.label: Medicines: all adjustments combined
rows.formula: evidence_adj * counterfactual_adj * attribution_share_shared * implementation_adj * leverage_funging_adj * wait_discount * med_missing_data_adj
rows.explainer: The medicines branch's adjustments.

rows.label: Grants: all adjustments combined
rows.formula: evidence_adj * counterfactual_adj * grt_attribution_share * grt_implementation_adj * leverage_funging_adj * wait_discount * grt_missing_data_adj
rows.explainer: The grants branch's adjustments.

rows.label: All adjustments combined (outcome-weighted average of the branches, for reading only)
rows.explainer: Outcome-weighted average of the branches, for reading only.

rows.label: Benefits and harms not modelled, as a share of modelled value
rows.explainer: Benefits: cold-chain support for partners' insulin and vaccines, emergency preparedness packs pre-positioned before hurricane season, mapping and data shared with responders (+). Harms: donated stock crowding out local suppliers, and the disposal burden of products that expire at partners (−). Net +5% (−10% to +15%).

rows.label: Deaths averted, in units of value
rows.formula: (people_reached * deaths_averted_per_person * med_total_adj + grt_deaths * grt_total_adj) * value_per_death + people_reached * ln_gain_per_person * $uov_per_ln_consumption * med_total_adj
rows.explainer: Deaths averted by both branches, each after its own adjustments, at the site's value of a death by age; no goods are valued as income.

rows.explainer: The bridge from units of value.

rows.label: WELLBYs (none)

rows.label: WELLBYs, as DALYs
rows.explainer: The bridge from WELLBYs.

rows.label: Illness averted, both branches, after adjustments, in DALYs
rows.explainer: Medicines and grants, each with its own adjustments.

rows.label: Years of healthy life (DALYs) averted in the year
rows.explainer: Both branches, plus the side effects at the shared weight.

rows.label: DALYs averted per dollar of Direct Relief's spending
rows.explainer: Outcome over cost.

rows.explainer: Convention 1: Direct Relief's pay and benefits over its cash expenses.

rows.explainer: The shared figure for US logistics and programme staff of a delivery organisation.
